 # Application Architecture

This document defines the foundational rules that keep the project coherent.
Consult it before changing the structure, content model, or publication flow.

## Execution Model

- The project is a static site generated by Hugo Extended.
- The Hugo version used for deployment is defined in
  `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` and must be respected locally.
- This repository has no application server, database, or proprietary API.
- A build produces static files that are published to GitHub Pages.
- The publication directory uses the base URL defined in `hugo.toml`,
  currently `https://www.gustavobelo.com/`.

Any proposal to introduce server-side state, persistence, authentication, or an
API must be treated as an architectural change and discussed before
implementation.

## Sources of Truth

Each type of change must have a clear source of truth:

| Responsibility | Source |
| --- | --- |
| Site configuration and theme parameters | `hugo.toml` |
| Pages, posts, and editorial metadata | `content/` |
| Templates and rendering behavior | `layouts/` |
| Authored CSS and JavaScript | `assets/` |
| Files copied without processing | `static/` |
| Supporting data and translations | `data/` and `i18n/` |
| Content import and transformation | `scripts/` |
| Automated guarantees | `tests/` |
| Deployment | `.github/workflows/` |
| Crawler and SEO policy (robots, sitemap) | `layouts/robots.txt`, `layouts/sitemap.xml`, `layouts/partials/head/` |

The published taxonomy is limited to `tags`, configured in `hugo.toml`.
Categories are not part of the site's content model or navigation.
The home page also publishes a JSON output used by the client-side Lunr search
index.

The `public/` and `resources/` directories contain generated artifacts. Never
edit these directories to fix the site; change the source and build it again.

## Content

- Editorial content must be versioned in `content/`, never directly in
  `public/`.
- Posts must follow the date and slug organization used in
  `content/posts/YYYY/MM/DD/slug/`.
- When a post has its own images, they must remain in the post's page bundle and
  be referenced through the shortcode or local resource convention used by the
  project.
- Front matter must preserve existing fields, especially `title`, `date`,
  `draft`, `tags`, and source identifiers when applicable.
- Existing URLs are part of the public contract. Changes to a slug, date, or
  `baseURL` require link verification and must be treated as compatibility
  changes.

## Presentation

- Hugo templates in `layouts/` are the page composition boundary.
- Reusable components should be implemented as partials or Hugo functions when
  the responsibility already belongs to the template system.
- CSS must originate from `assets/css/style.scss` and its imports; do not edit
  minified or generated CSS in `public/`.
- Theme colors must be defined as Sass variables in
  `assets/css/_variables.scss`, using the existing light and dark variants and
  `!default` values as the project defaults. New styles must reuse these
  variables instead of introducing hard-coded theme colors; palette changes
  belong in the variables file.
- Authored JavaScript must originate from `assets/js/`; published minified
  files are build outputs.
- Third-party resources must use the asset, CDN, and configuration mechanisms
  already used by the theme. A new dependency must justify its cost, origin,
  and build impact.

## SEO and Crawling

- The site language/locale is configured with the top-level `locale` key in
  `hugo.toml` (currently `pt-BR`). Templates must read it through
  `.Site.Language.Locale`, not the deprecated `.Site.LanguageCode`.
- `robots.txt` is generated from `layouts/robots.txt` and requires
  `enableRobotsTXT = true` in `hugo.toml`. It must keep allowing crawling and
  rendering assets (no blanket `Disallow` for `*`) and must keep the
  `Sitemap:` line.
- The current policy for AI bots is to allow on-demand/search crawlers
  (`OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `Claude-SearchBot`, `Claude-User`,
  `PerplexityBot`) and disallow training-only crawlers (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`,
  `Google-Extended`, `CCBot`, `Applebot-Extended`). Changing this stance is an
  editorial/product decision, not a routine fix; confirm with the site owner
  before adding or removing bots from either group.
- Per-page metadata (title, description, canonical, Open Graph, Twitter Card,
  JSON-LD) is composed in `layouts/partials/head/`. Keep new metadata fields
  consistent with the existing `params.seo.*` and front matter conventions
  instead of introducing a parallel mechanism.
- List pages (home, section, taxonomy, term) reuse one `Page` for every
  paginated URL, so `.Permalink` always resolves to page 1. The canonical tag
  in `layouts/partials/head/link.html` must use the active `.Paginator.URL`
  for page 2+ instead of `.Permalink`.
- Taxonomy term pages get a generated description (`layouts/partials/function/description.html`)
  instead of the generic site default, and a term page backing fewer than 2
  posts is marked `noindex, follow` in `layouts/_default/baseof.html` to keep
  thin, single-post tag pages out of search results.
- Post images render through `layouts/partials/plugin/image.html`, which uses
  a JS-driven (lazysizes) placeholder swap for real browsers. It must keep a
  `<noscript>` fallback with the real `src`/`srcset` and native
  `loading="lazy"` so crawlers that don't execute JavaScript can still see and
  index the image.

## Build and Publication

The official workflow is:

1. Change the source files.
2. Run a local build with the relevant deployment parameters.
3. Run the tests in `tests/` when the change affects importing or rendering.
4. Push to `main` only after reviewing the diff.
5. The GitHub Actions workflow runs on pushes to `main` or manually, runs
  `hugo --gc --minify`, and publishes `public/` to the `gh-pages` branch.
6. Configure GitHub Pages to deploy from the `gh-pages` branch root.

Do not include `public/` in authored commits because it is recreated by the
deployment.

## Rules for AI Use

- AI must locate the correct source of truth before editing any file.
- AI must not edit generated artifacts, rewrite the entire theme, or introduce
  an unnecessary abstraction layer.
- Layout, configuration, content, script, and test changes must remain separate
  according to `.github/COMMIT_GUIDELINES.md`.
- After a change, AI must run the check closest to the risk:
  `hugo --buildDrafts` for rendering and `python3 -m pytest -q` for contracts
  covered by the tests.
- When unsure about a public URL, asset location, front matter, language, or
  expected behavior, AI must ask before choosing a new convention.

## Architectural Changes

Treat any change as architectural when it:

- changes the content model or URL structure;
- introduces an external service, API, database, or client-side state;
- changes the build or deployment mechanism or the main Hugo version;
- replaces the boundary between `layouts/`, `assets/`, and `static/`; or
- changes the image storage or processing strategy.

Architectural changes must update this document and include tests or a
reproducible check that demonstrates the new contract.

The validation procedure for this rule is defined in
`.github/skills/architecture-validation/SKILL.md`.
